name: Sahm unemployment gap rule
research_question: Has the three-month average US unemployment rate risen by at least the configured threshold relative to its prior 12-month low?
primary_reference: Claudia Sahm, Direct Stimulus Payments to Broadly Support the Economy, Brookings/Hamilton Project, March 2019
original_universe: United States civilian unemployment rate (U-3), seasonally adjusted
formula_specification: Three-month moving average of the unemployment rate minus the minimum three-month average over the prior 12 months, excluding the current month; trigger when the gap is at or above 0.50 percentage points in the published rule.
data_requirements: Monthly US seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate in percent
At least 15 contiguous months for one evaluation
Consistent geography, frequency and seasonal adjustment across inputs
assumptions: Inputs are validated economic observations, not derived features
Month boundaries follow calendar month starts
limitations: Association with recessions already under way; not an NBER determination
Not a forward recession forecast or investment signal
Independent academic replication not claimed until a reference example is matched
